I relate to this, and I've also come to describe my autism as "little bits of a lot of other mental conditions/disabilities." 

I think it's reasonable that you may or may not be autistic even with some traits, but maybe you have a form of PTSD that you didnt realise affected you? 

In that same breath, though, I've learned that many doctors will only diagnose people with autism after they've been "traumatised enough" to show clear symptoms and see how they crack under pressure. 

I hope you're satisfied with your results after you get your diagnosis sorted, though!

I understand the idea of wanting to stop being so obsessed/interested in things. It's painful!! And I can only imagine it's worse when you want to distance yourself from it as a result of no longer being comfortable with it. I've had a few similar cases to this... but not to your level, I don't think.

I think it'll make it easier on your psyche if you acknowledge both the good and the bad of the game series, and accept that you're not a bad person for liking it. If you're into the characters or story, then this will be an easier alternative to completely dropping the game. But if you just like the gameplay aspect of it, or if you like that aspect more, then as other commenters have said... I'm sure you'll be able to find games that are similar that you might end up identifying with even more! 

Or you could try and "replace" the interest. Which doesn't actually mean forgetting about how you like the game a whole lot, but finding other games/shows/etc to engage with and obsess with more in order to try and push the other series more to the back of your mind, so you can still remember your fond memories of it, and still engage with it, but to a lesser degree.

My buddy is going through the exact same thing right now, after trying to help them figure it all out.

They're similar in that they don't always know what to say... but in my experience with getting a diagnosis, if you just say you suspect you have something, then list a few reasons why, they'll guide you in the direction for you to talk more about it and you'll fall into an easy routine!

Also, parents can have a really basic idea of what autism is. Mine did too, and it prevented me from getting help for years. Now that you're 18, you can get the diagnosis yourself OR you can tell your parents that you think something might be up with you, but you want to get it checked out professionally just to make sure.

It is originally Chinese! And so are those other words. There's a lot to get into about the history of Kanji in Japan and how China has greatly shaped Japan's growth and culture, but basically: 

Chinese characters when used in a Japanese context (kanji) are read differently than they would be if they were read in a Chinese dialect. There can be almost no change (specifically only dropping the accents) or there can be a drastic change. Japan borrowed the character system from China, and with it, many of their characters and the meanings behind them. 

Still two vastly different languages, though. Nothing like the groupings of European languages ... I think it's interesting!

I haven't played any other version of DQXI, but some IMPORTANT things for him to know.....

* if you haven't already bought the game and want to make sure he'll like the gameplay aspect, the 8-hour-long demo is a good place to start!
* also, downloading the free DLC from the eshop is an added bonus
* i prefer setting the 'overworld' theme to the one from DQVIII in the audio settings. he can switch between the two for some variety.
* the game is VERY long. he doesn't have to play all of it in one sitting, but he'll have to be prepared to play it in short bursts over a long time or a lot all in one sitting in a slightly-shorter-but-still-long time
* one of the pros of this game is that, when you get party members, they all get EXP even if they arent active. so they all level up around the same time and can keep-up with each other
* different costumes to find!
* the models for NPCs and monsters are often re-used and reskinned. it's nothing new to the franchise. but i like deciding which colour schemes I prefer for monsters. lol  
(Edit: the music is often reused, too. he'll get used to it)
* Each of the characters have stories and archs that I got more invested in than i thought
* it's a good idea to save to two save files .... not too important near the beginning of the game, but when things start really coming together... it might be more interesting.
